To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

EBV-specific CTLs with reduced sensitivity to the Fas/Fas ligand-mediated death pathway were generated by transducing them with siRNA that targets Fas mRNA and that this manipulation had no discernible effect on their growth and function.
we have developed a method to make T cells resistant to apoptosis induced by FasL and we have demonstrated that the modified cells retain their antiviral and antitumor activity.
we have shown that EBV-specific cytolytic T cells (CTLs) can be modified to resist apoptosis mediated by the Fas/Fas ligand (Fas/FasL) death pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of EBV-specific cytolytic T lymphocytes (CTLs) that have been modified to resist apoptosis induced by the death receptor, Fas.
the development of EBV-specific CTLs for use in immunotherapy of EBV-associated tumors.
developing strategies to improve the efficacy of EBV-specific CTLs in the treatment of EBV-associated tumors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Fas down-modulation by siRNA can be achieved in human EBV-CTL and the modified cells can resist Fas/Fas ligand-mediated apoptosis.

the knock down of Fas expression in EBV- CTLs is a useful strategy to protect EBV-CTL cells against FasL-mediated cell death and to enhance the efficacy of EBV-CTL cell therapy for EBV-associated tumors.
Fas down-modulation is a safe and effective method to render CTLs resistant to Fas/Fas-ligand-mediated apoptosis and that the Fas(low) phenotype is not associated with any other functional defect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a strategy to render EBV-specific cytolytic T cells resistant to Fas-mediated killing by EBV-positive tumors.
the EBV-specific CTLs are a promising candidate for adoptive cellular immunotherapy of NPC.

we have developed a strategy for the modification of T cells to resist a single apoptotic signal, without altering the physiologic growth and survival requirements of these cells, and that the modified cells retain their antitumor function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Fas expression can be down-modulated in EBV- specific cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) without affecting other physiologic properties of the cells.
it is possible to knockdown the Fas receptor in T cells using siRNA technology and that these modified T cells are more resistant to apoptosis induced by Fas/Fas-ligand interaction.
EBV-CTL can be rendered resistant to Fas-mediated apoptosis by transduction with siRNA.
